compound_and_chemistry: ARC-520 Injection — an RNAi (siRNA) therapeutic against HBV, supplied as two vials mixed at the bedside by a study pharmacist. (1) API: "a 1:1 molar mixture of 2 synthetic, double-stranded, cholesterol-conjugated RNA oligonucleotides" — RNAi triggers AD0009 and AD0010. The paper states the triggers "were chemically modified using sugar and backbone analogues to increase nuclease resistance and minimize the potential for induction of an innate immune response." (2) Delivery excipient ARC-EX1: "a masked, hepatocyte-targeted polymeric amine (polymeric amine = l-melittin-derived peptide; masking group = carboxydimethyl maleic anhydride N-acetyl galactosamine [NAG-MLP])". SEQUENCES ARE PUBLISHED, in full, in Table 1 ("Cholesterol-RNAi Triggers AD0009 and AD0010 Used in the Study"): AD0009 sense Chol-Au CfuGfuAfgGfcAfuAfaAfuUfgGfuAf(invdT), antisense dTAfcCfaAfuUfuAfuGfcCfuAfcAfg dTsdT; AD0010 sense Chol-uAu AfcCfuCfuGfcCfuAfaUfcAfuCfuAf(invdT), antisense dTAfgAfuGfaUfuAfgGfcAfgAfgGfu dTsdT. The notation shows 2'-modified (f-suffixed) sugars, deoxy residues, an inverted-dT 3' cap on the sense strands and a phosphorothioate linkage in the antisense dTsdT overhang; the paper does not spell out the modification identities in prose, so the precise assignment of "f" to 2'-fluoro is my reading of the table notation, not an explicit statement.
dose_route_schedule: Single-dose, intravenous, first-in-human sequential dose escalation — no repeat dosing. Nine cohorts, 6 subjects each, 4:2 active:placebo. Doses: 0.01, 0.1, 0.3, 0.6, 1.2, 2.0 (cohort 6), 2.0 (cohort 7), 3.0, 4.0 mg/kg. Placebo = 0.9% normal saline. INFUSION DURATION IS GIVEN AS RATE, NOT TIME (Table 2, "Dose and Infusion Rates for Cohorts 1-9"): cohorts 1-2 "Slow push" (footnote: "Initial volumes for cohorts 1-2 were too small to administer using syringe pump infusion as planned in the protocol; thus, they were given by slow push"); cohort 3 at 7 mL/min; cohorts 4-6 at 3.5 mL/min; cohorts 7-9 at 2 mL/min. Footnote: "The infusion rate for cohorts 7-9 was reduced from 3.5 to 2 mL/min at the overlapping dose of 2 mg/kg to lessen risk of infusion reaction." Elapsed infusion time in minutes is NOT reported. Cohorts 7-9 only received pretreatment with oral diphenhydramine 50 mg, at least 2 hours before study drug. This rate-reduction plus antihistamine design is directly relevant: the infusion-rate de-escalation was a response to hypersensitivity, and complement was one of the readouts tracked across it.
complement_analytes: Exactly TWO complement analytes, and the lead's claim is CONFIRMED verbatim. From the Pharmacodynamic Assessments / Complement methods: "Venous blood samples were collected and processed to produce serum (for complement CH50 analysis) or plasma (for split products-Bb analysis)." So: (1) Bb — the alternative-pathway activation split product (factor B fragment Bb), measured in PLASMA; the Results call it "a measure of alternative pathway activation". (2) CH50 — total complement hemolytic activity (classical-pathway functional assay), measured in SERUM. No C3a, C5a, C4d, SC5b-9/sTCC, C3, C4, Bb/C3bBb complexes or deposition readouts were measured. Sampling schedule for complement: "Initially the 0- (pre-) and 0.5-hour postdose samples were analyzed, with the remaining samples analyzed if a change from baseline was observed at 0.5 hours" — i.e. a conditional/triggered analysis scheme, not all-timepoints-in-all-subjects. (Separately, cytokines IL-6, MCP-1, TNF-alpha, IL-8, IL-1beta, IFN-alpha, MIP-1alpha were run in serum by Luminex; those are not complement.)
matrix_and_anticoagulant: DUAL MATRIX, EXPLICITLY STATED AND VERIFIED — this is the notable feature of this paper. Serum for CH50; plasma for Bb, in one sentence: "Venous blood samples were collected and processed to produce serum (for complement CH50 analysis) or plasma (for split products-Bb analysis)." ANTICOAGULANT FOR THE COMPLEMENT PLASMA IS NOT REPORTED. There is no anticoagulant named anywhere in the complement methods, and no mention of citrate, EDTA-futhan, or any complement-stabilising collection tube. CAUTION AGAINST A MISREAD: the article does name EDTA, but only in the bioanalytical/pharmacokinetic methods, for the PK plasma samples ("...acid (EDTA) as an anticoagulant. Samples were centrifuged at 4 degrees C, and plasma was stored at -20 degrees C until transfer to the bioanalytical laboratory. Plasma samples were assayed by a validated liquid chromatography with fluorescence detection method for the ARC-520 siRNAs"). That EDTA statement belongs to the siRNA PK assay and must NOT be carried over to the Bb plasma; the paper never links them. Also note an internal inconsistency worth recording: the Discussion says innate immune activation "was assessed through measurement of complement and cytokine activation in plasma," which contradicts the Methods (CH50 in serum, cytokines in serum). The Methods statement is the specific one and should be treated as authoritative.
assay_and_vendor: NOT REPORTED. No kit, platform, manufacturer or reference laboratory is named for either CH50 or Bb. The methods say only that samples were sent to "the bioanalytical laboratory" (unnamed in the complement context). By contrast the paper does name vendors elsewhere (Luminex for the cytokine panel; Phoenix WinNonlin 6.3, Certara/Pharsight for PK; SAS 9.2, SAS Institute for statistics; Panagene for the PNA probes; Petrus Pharmaceuticals for the diphenhydramine) — so the omission is specific to the complement assays. No CH50 units (e.g. CAE units, U/mL) and no Bb units are given. UNVERIFIED for vendor, kit, platform, assay units, LLOQ and reference ranges.
n_subjects: Enrolled/dosed: 54 healthy adult volunteers, half male and half female — 36 ARC-520 Injection, 18 placebo (registry actual enrollment also 54, so publication and registry agree). Structure: 9 cohorts x 6 subjects, randomized 4:2 active:placebo; cohorts 1-6 and 8-9 opened with a 2-subject sentinel group (1 active, 1 placebo) reviewed by the DSMC through day 3 before the remaining 4 were dosed. Follow-up: "35 of 36 persons in the ARC-520 Injection treatment group and 17 of 18 in the placebo group continued through their day 90 follow-up call" (1 treatment withdrawal for personal reasons, 1 placebo withdrawal for travel conflicts; no discontinuations for adverse events). Safety analysis population: "All study subjects receiving any test article were included in the safety analyses" (= 54). NUMBER WITH COMPLEMENT ACTUALLY MEASURED IS NOT EXPLICITLY STATED — UNVERIFIED. The paper defines a PK population ("Samples of all subjects were analyzed"; "Pharmacokinetic data were presented for all subjects who were administered ARC-520 Injection") but never defines a pharmacodynamic/complement analysis population or gives an n for CH50 or Bb. The conditional sampling scheme (only pre-dose and 0.5 h analyzed first, later timepoints only "if a change from baseline was observed at 0.5 hours") means the number of subjects with a full complement time course is certainly below 54 and is nowhere reported. It is inferable that all 54 had at least the pre-dose and 0.5-h draws, because results are reported as cohort averages across cohorts 3-9 and include placebo recipients, but that inference is mine and is not stated. Do not record a complement denominator as 54 or 36 without flagging it as inferred.
result_direction: POSITIVE / SIGNAL PRESENT, but low-level, transient, and judged not clinically significant by the authors. Two distinct directional findings. (1) Bb (alternative pathway) INCREASED: sporadic individual increases starting at 0.3 mg/kg (cohort 3, 1 subject) and 0.6 mg/kg (cohort 4, 1 subject), becoming a cohort-average pattern at the four highest-exposure groups (cohorts 6, 7, 8, 9 = 2.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0 mg/kg), i.e. an apparent dose/exposure relationship. Timing: "In all cases, the increase in Bb occurred at 0.5 and 2 hours postdose." Magnitude bounded only by a negative statement: no subject reached the pre-specified 4-fold clinical-significance threshold. (2) CH50 DECREASED (consumption direction): a pattern toward decrease at 2 hours postdose in cohort 9 (4.0 mg/kg) in 4 subjects — but 3 active AND 1 PLACEBO, which weakens attribution to drug. All changes resolved by 6 hours post-dose. Author interpretation: "Low-level complement increases were all transient and minimal, indicating that their clinical consequence would be questionable... this indicates that ARC-520 Injection has a low potential to activate the innate immune system." Abstract: "Low-level, transient complement induction and sporadic, mild, and transient elevations of several cytokines were observed but not associated with any symptoms." Context: the study's prominent safety finding was 2 moderate hypersensitivity reactions attributed to mast-cell/histamine release, NOT to complement; in vitro work (Figure 2, rat peritoneal mast cells) supported the histamine mechanism. So complement activation was detected but was not advanced as the mechanism of the clinical reactions.
result_verbatim: Results, "Complement": "An increase in individual Bb levels (a measure of alternative pathway activation) was detected beginning in cohort 3 (1 subject) and cohort 4 (1 subject). A pattern of Bb increase was seen in the cohort average for groups 6, 7, 8, and 9. Increases were mild, with no subject having a 4-fold or greater increase over baseline, which would be considered clinically significant. In all cases, the increase in Bb occurred at 0.5 and 2 hours postdose. In addition, in cohort 9, there was a pattern toward a decrease in CH50 at 2 hours postdose in 4 subjects (3 treated with ARC-520 Injection, 1 treated with placebo). All changes had resolved by 6 hours after dosing." Methods: "Venous blood samples were collected and processed to produce serum (for complement CH50 analysis) or plasma (for split products-Bb analysis)."
values_location: NOT REPORTED AS NUMBERS ANYWHERE — narrative text only. I enumerated every table-wrap and fig element in the PMC JATS XML. The complete inventory is: Table 1 (Cholesterol-RNAi Triggers AD0009 and AD0010), Table 2 (Dose and Infusion Rates for Cohorts 1-9), Table 3 (Incidence of Adverse Events), Table 4 (Summary of Pharmacokinetic Parameters), Table 5 (Dose Proportionality, log-log regression), Figure 1 (study flow diagram), Figure 2 (in vitro rat peritoneal mast cell histamine release), Figure 3 (mean plasma concentration-time profiles for MLP and the two siRNAs). NONE of these is a complement table or figure. There is no complement figure, no complement table, no mean/SD, no fold-change value, no per-cohort number, no units and no p-value for CH50 or Bb. The only quantitative anchor is the negative bound "no subject having a 4-fold or greater increase over baseline." Supplementary material was checked via the Europe PMC supplementaryFiles endpoint (HTTP 200, 298 KB zip): it contains only the three figure image files (CPDD-6-350-g001/g002/g003 as .jpg and .gif) — i.e. the already-published Figures 1-3, with NO additional complement data. The word "supplement" does not occur anywhere in the article body. Consequence for the inventory: this trial supports a qualitative/directional complement entry only; it cannot contribute extractable numeric complement values.
is_registered_outcome: PROTOCOL SAFETY/PHARMACODYNAMIC ANALYSIS — NOT a registered outcome measure. Verified against the ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 record for NCT01872065. The outcomesModule contains exactly one primary outcome ("To determine the incidence and frequency of adverse events as a measure of safety and tolerability of ARC-520") and exactly one secondary outcome ("To evaluate the pharmacokinetics of ARC-520 at different dose concentrations" — Cmax, tmax, AUC0-24, AUCinf, t1/2). Complement, CH50, Bb, pharmacodynamics and innate immunity appear NOWHERE in either outcome measure or its description. However, complement was clearly protocol-specified rather than incidental: the publication lists it as a pre-planned pharmacodynamic endpoint ("Blood samples were collected predose and at specified times after dosing to determine pharmacokinetic (PK) parameters and pharmacodynamic (PD) end points (cytokines and complement)"), with a pre-specified conditional sampling scheme, a pre-specified 4-fold clinical-significance threshold, and a dedicated Methods subsection. So it is stronger than an incidental safety lab but weaker than a registered outcome measure. RESULTS ARE NOT POSTED: the API response has hasResults = false and no resultsSection, despite the study being COMPLETED since 2014-11 and the record having been updated as recently as 2025-12-26. There is therefore no registry results table to cross-check or to recover numeric complement values from.
counting_rationale: COUNT IT as a new verified human clinical trial with measured complement. All four criteria are met first-hand: (1) human — 54 healthy adult volunteers; (2) a real registered interventional trial — NCT01872065 / Heparc-1001, Phase 1, randomized, double-blind (quadruple-masked), placebo-controlled, confirmed in the registry API; (3) a therapeutic oligonucleotide — ARC-520 Injection, a cholesterol-conjugated siRNA pair with published sequences; (4) complement was actually MEASURED, as a pre-planned pharmacodynamic endpoint, with two analytes (Bb, CH50) and a reported result. NOT an efficacy readout: the drug targets HBV cccDNA-derived mRNA transcripts, so complement here is purely a safety / innate-immune-activation toxicity readout. The target_is_complement_efficacy caveat does NOT apply. Count it ONCE, and keep it distinct from the ARC-520 chronic-HBV patient studies (the Heparc-2001 Phase 2, cited as reference 37 in this paper) — this lead is the healthy-volunteer Phase 1 only. Carry these three qualifiers into the inventory so the entry is not overstated: (a) complement is NOT a registered outcome measure and no results are posted on ClinicalTrials.gov; (b) the complement denominator is NOT stated, and the conditional sampling scheme means fewer than 54 subjects have a full time course — do not assert n=54 or n=36 for complement; (c) ZERO numeric complement values exist in the paper or its supplement, so this is a directional/qualitative data point (Bb up dose-relatedly at >=0.3 mg/kg and in cohort averages at 2.0-4.0 mg/kg; CH50 down at 2 h in cohort 9 but in 1 placebo subject too; all resolved by 6 h; none exceeding the 4-fold threshold). The dual-matrix design (serum CH50 / plasma Bb) is confirmed and is a genuinely useful methodological datapoint, but the plasma anticoagulant is unreported, which limits its value as a methods exemplar.
still_needed: Four gaps, all of which would require non-public sources: (1) complement assay vendor, kit, platform, units, LLOQ and reference ranges for CH50 and Bb — entirely unnamed; (2) the anticoagulant and collection-tube type for the Bb plasma (do NOT infer EDTA from the PK methods); (3) the actual complement denominator — how many of the 54 had Bb and CH50 measured, and how many had post-0.5 h timepoints run under the conditional scheme; (4) numeric complement values (per-cohort mean/SD or fold-change for Bb and CH50). None of these is recoverable from the publication, its figures, its supplementary files (figure images only), or the registry (no results posted, hasResults=false). Plausible remaining public routes not yet exhausted, if the orchestrator wants them pursued: the companion Phase 2 publication in chronic-HBV patients (reference 37: Yuen M, Chan H, Given B, et al., "Phase II, dose ranging study of ARC-520...") may report complement with numbers; and reference 18 (the ARC-520 trigger-selection/NAG-MLP paper) may carry preclinical complement data. An FDA/EMA review package is unlikely to help since ARC-520 was discontinued and never approved, so there should be no approved-product review on accessdata. No paywall, login, CAPTCHA or technical block was encountered at any point in this verification; every route returned the needed content on the first attempt.

compound_and_chemistry:
Eight unique GalNAc3-conjugated phosphorothioate 2'-O-methoxyethyl (2'MOE) chimeric "gapmer" antisense oligonucleotides, all 20-mers of 5-10-5 MOE design, conjugated to triantennary N-acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc3, denoted "L-" at the 5' end) for ASGR1-mediated hepatocyte uptake. Backbone is either full phosphorothioate (PS) or mixed phosphodiester/phosphorothioate (PO/PS).

SEQUENCES ARE PUBLISHED IN FULL (Table 1), with Ionis compound ID numbers — there are NO NCT numbers, so these IDs are the only compound-level identifiers:
- ApoC3 / APOC3, ION 678354, L-AGCTTCTTGTCCAGCTTTAT, 20, 5-10-5 MOE (PS)
- LPA / apo(a), ION 681257, L-TGCTCCGTTGGTGCTTGTTC, 20, 5-10-5 MOE (PO/PS)
- CFB / complement factor B, ION 696844, L-ATCCCACGCCCCTGTCCAGC, 20, 5-10-5 MOE (PS)
- ANGPTL3, ION 703802, L-GGACATTGCCAGTAATCGCA, 20, 5-10-5 MOE (PO/PS)
- HBV S (hepatitis B surface antigen), ION 712408, L-GCAGAGGTGAAGCGAAGTGC, 20, 5-10-5 MOE (PS)
- KLKB1 (prekallikrein), ION 721744, L-TGCAAGTCTCTTGGCAAACA, 20, 5-10-5 MOE (PO/PS) — footnote b: "Data not included in primary integrated analyses (monthly dose ranging pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics only)"
- AGT (angiotensinogen), ION 757456, L-CACAAACAAGCTGGTCGGTT, 20, 5-10-5 MOE (PS)
- GHR (growth hormone receptor), ION 766720, L-CCACCTTTGGGTGAATAGCA, 20, 5-10-5 MOE (PO/PS)

CRITICAL CONFOUND: ION 696844 targets CFB (complement factor B). For that one compound complement is the EFFICACY target — the paper lists "FB-L" among the four conjugates with "[d]irectly assayable plasma analytes ... to assess pharmacodynamic effects". Bb is itself the activation fragment of factor B, so in FB-L recipients Bb can fall for pharmacologic (on-target) reasons. The complement safety data are POOLED across ASOs (each figure point = "at least 10 subjects and 3 GalNAc3-conjugated 2'MOE ASOs"; Supp Table S7 baseline rows state "Number of ASOs: 7"), and FB-L is one of the contributing ASOs. The paper never separates FB-L from the others in any complement table or figure. See "target_is_complement_efficacy" caveat in counting_rationale.
n_subjects:
ENROLLED/RANDOMIZED (Table 1, across all eight compounds): 392 total = 98 placebo + 294 active.
EXCLUDED from primary integrated analyses: KLKB1 / ION 721744 (n = 32; 8 placebo + 24 active), per Table 1 footnote b.
ANALYSED COHORTS: weekly multidose regimen cohort N = 157 (Table 5 title: "Incidence of Abnormal Laboratory Test Results in Weekly Multidose Regimen Cohort (N = 157)"); single-dose regimen cohort N = 193 (Supp Table S9: "Incidence of abnormal laboratory test results in the single-dose regimen cohort (N=193)"). 157 + 193 = 350. Note an unreconciled discrepancy: 392 enrolled minus 32 KLKB1 = 360, which is 10 more than 350; the paper does not explain the gap. Flagged, not resolved.

NUMBER WITH COMPLEMENT ACTUALLY MEASURED (denominators differ by analyte — C5a was measured in fewer subjects than Bb):
- Multidose cohort (Table 5): Bb n = 36 placebo / 121 total ASO (dose strata 32, 38, 33, 12, 6) = 157. C5a n = 30 placebo / 97 total ASO (dose strata 20, 26, 33, 12, 6) = 127.
- Single-dose cohort (Supp Table S9): Bb n = 50 placebo / 142 total ASO (29, 15, 32, 21, 45) = 192. C5a n = 44 placebo / 124 total ASO (23, 9, 26, 21, 45) = 168.

dose_route_schedule:
Route: subcutaneous (SC) injection in all protocols — "The route of study drug administration was by SC injection in all protocols." NOT intravenous, so there is no infusion duration and no infusion-rate variable. This matters for the endpoint: complement activation-related pseudoallergy (CARPA) in oligonucleotides is classically an IV-infusion phenomenon, so an all-SC dataset is a weak test of that mechanism.

Doses: "Single doses of 5-120 mg and multiple doses of 10-120 mg were evaluated in these studies. The multiple dose regimens included six weekly SC doses (Supplementary Table S2), and we also evaluated monthly doses for the GalNAc3-conjugated 2'MOE ASOs."
Dose strata used throughout: placebo, >0-10, >10-20, >20-40, >40-60, >60 mg/week.
Per-compound multidose schedules (Supp Table S2): QW, BIW, 3qod-QW, and 2BIW-QW regimens over 4-8 doses across study weeks 1-6.
Complement sampling: predose plus several timepoints within 24 h after the FIRST SC dose only — sampled at Screening, Baseline, and 2, 3, 4, 8, 12, 24 h after Day 1 dosing (per Fig. 9 x-axis and Supp Table S7 timepoint rows). There is NO complement sampling after later doses, so no assessment of complement activation on repeat exposure.
complement_analytes:
CONFIRMED — the prior search record is CORRECT. Exactly two analytes: Bb and C5a, both explicitly called complement split products.

Methods verbatim: "...coagulation (activated partial thromboplastin time and prothrombin time) and complement activation (complement split products Bb and C5a)."
Fig. 9 legend verbatim: "(c) complement split product Bb, and (d) complement split product C5a."
Units: Bb in µg/mL; C5a in ng/mL.

NOT measured: C3, C4, C3a, C5b-9/sC5b-9, CH50, AH50, Bb/C3 ratios, properdin, factor H, any functional assay, any deposition assay. There is no total-complement or classical-pathway readout at all. Coverage is alternative pathway (Bb) plus terminal anaphylatoxin (C5a) only.
matrix_and_anticoagulant:
NOT REPORTED. The source omits this entirely.

The only sampling statement is: "Samples were collected before dosing for standard clinical laboratory tests and collected at several time points within a 24-h period after SC dose administration for coagulation tests and complement split products." No matrix is named for Bb or C5a — not serum, not plasma, not whole blood. No anticoagulant is named. No sample-handling, chilling, or processing detail is given, which is a material omission for complement split products (Bb and especially C5a are notoriously sensitive to ex vivo activation and to anticoagulant choice; EDTA vs citrate vs serum changes the values).

Verified absent by three independent routes: (1) grep of the Europe PMC full-text XML — the only "plasma" hits concern the ASO PK bioanalytical assay, and the only "serum" hits are "serum creatinine"; (2) grep of the 53-page supplementary PDF — "serum" appears only in "Serum Creatinine" rows; (3) WebFetch of the PMC HTML, which returned "The article does not specify the biological matrix, anticoagulant, or assay method/vendor/kit used to measure Bb and C5a." I also inspected the Figure 9 image directly: panel c is labelled only "Bb (µg/mL), Mean +/- SEM" and panel d only "C5a (ng/mL), Mean +/- SEM" — no matrix on the axes either.
assay_and_vendor:
NOT REPORTED / UNVERIFIED. No assay method, platform, kit, vendor, catalogue number, central laboratory, LLOQ, or validation statement is given for Bb or C5a anywhere in the main text, the Methods, the figure legends, or the 53-page supplement. (By contrast the paper DOES describe the ASO bioanalytical method in detail — a hybridization-ligation ELISA performed under 21 CFR Part 58 — so the omission for complement is selective, not a general style of the paper.)

THRESHOLDS (these are reported): event criterion for both Bb and C5a is ">2 x ULN, or BSLN if >ULN" (Table 5 and Supp Table S9). Reference ranges are medians of the individual studies (Supp Table S1): Bb LLN 0.49, ULN 1.42 µg/mL (single-dose) / 1.49 µg/mL (multidose); C5a LLN 0.37, ULN 74.33 ng/mL. Methods state the ranges "represent the median values" across studies, and "If there was no reference range available, then the range was calculated as the (mean +/-2 x SD) of the baseline values in the data set" — so the ULNs are partly data-derived rather than assay-anchored, which is a further reason the missing assay identity matters.
is_registered_outcome:
Protocol safety analysis — and specifically a POOLED, retrospectively integrated safety analysis, not a registered outcome measure. Complement split products were prospectively collected per protocol at defined post-dose timepoints, and events were adjudicated against thresholds "as defined by protocol stopping rules, standard reporting, or Grade 3 criteria provided by the Food and Drug Administration in Guidance to Industry for healthy adults and adolescents", which establishes that Bb/C5a were pre-specified protocol safety labs in the underlying trials.

However, registration status of this endpoint is UNVERIFIED and unverifiable from this source: no registry identifiers exist in the paper, so no registered outcome-measure list can be checked against it. result_direction:
NEGATIVE AS REPORTED (no complement activation signal), but with two documented exceptions that the main text does not mention and that should not be laundered into a clean null.

Headline: no effect on Bb or C5a relative to baseline over 24 h after the first dose, in either the single-dose or multidose cohort, at any dose stratum up to >60 mg/week. Main-text Table 5 (multidose, N=157) shows 0 (0.0%) events for both Bb and C5a in every group including placebo.

Exception 1 — incidence: in the SINGLE-dose cohort (Supp Table S9, not the main text), Bb exceeded the 2 x ULN criterion in 1 ASO-treated subject (1/142, 0.7%; located in the >0-10 mg stratum, 1/29 = 3.4%) AND in 1 placebo subject (1/50, 2.0%). So the placebo rate numerically exceeded the ASO rate, which supports the null, but the literal claim of zero excursions is true only of the multidose cohort. C5a had 0 events in every group in both cohorts.

Exception 2 — inferential: Supp Table S7 carries exactly one significance marker in the entire complement table — Bb, Day 1 12 h, >0-10 mg/wk group, *p < 0.05 for change from baseline vs placebo (mean 1.63 µg/mL [SD 1.31, SEM 0.26] vs placebo 1.62 [1.17, 0.19]). The group means are essentially identical; the nominal significance arises from the change-from-baseline contrast (that stratum's baseline was 1.13 vs placebo 1.39). It is unadjusted for multiplicity across 7 dose strata x 8 timepoints x 2 analytes, it is in the LOWEST dose group with no dose-response, and it is not flagged or discussed anywhere in the paper. I report it because it exists, not because I think it is real.

Direction caveat: because Bb is the cleavage fragment of factor B and one of the seven pooled ASOs (ION 696844) targets CFB for knockdown, any true Bb decrease in the pooled data could be on-target pharmacology rather than absence of toxicity. Pooling makes this unresolvable from the published data.

counting_rationale:
THE REVIEW'S ASSERTION IS WRONG AND MUST BE CORRECTED. This paper unambiguously reports human complement measurement (Bb and C5a split products) in healthy volunteers dosed with GalNAc3-conjugated 2'MOE ASOs. The claim that the GalNAc-conjugated generation has NO human complement measurement at all cannot survive this source. The prior search record ("measured Bb and C5a, described as 'complement split product' in a figure legend") is verified verbatim and first-hand. The EMA-assessment-report route that produced the original assertion simply missed this; it is a sponsor-authored integrated analysis in Nucleic Acid Therapeutics, not a regulatory document.

HOW IT SHOULD BE COUNTED — this is a middle case, and I want to be precise rather than convenient:

It is MORE recoverable than Crooke 2016. Crooke 2016 pooled 52 trials and >2,600 subjects with essentially no compound-level recovery. Here, Table 1 names all eight compounds individually with Ionis ID numbers, full 20-mer sequences, backbone chemistry, design, and per-compound placebo/active/total denominators; Supplementary Table S2 names six individual multidose trials with their dose schedules; and the column header "Phase 1 HV-RCT, n" implies one phase 1 healthy-volunteer RCT per compound.

But it is STILL a pooled assessment for this endpoint, for three independent reasons:
1. No trial identities. Zero NCT numbers, zero protocol codes, zero registry references anywhere in the paper or its supplement. The trials cannot be looked up, cross-checked against registered outcome measures, or deduplicated against other publications. The paper never even states how many trials there are.
2. The complement data themselves are pooled across compounds. Every complement data point aggregates "at least 10 subjects and 3 GalNAc3-conjugated 2'MOE ASOs"; Supp Table S7 reports a varying "Number of ASOs" per cell (1 to 7). No per-trial or per-compound complement result is recoverable for ANY of the eight compounds.
3. The pooling is explicitly post hoc (individual study datasets merged into one SAS dataset; ANCOVA with trial as a factor).

RECOMMENDED COUNTING: count this as ONE verified human complement-measurement dataset in GalNAc3-conjugated ASOs — covering 7 compounds and roughly 350 subjects with Bb, ~294-348 with C5a depending on timepoint — and do NOT count it as 6, 7, or 8 separately verified trials. Counting it as multiple trials would assert trial identities the source does not supply. If the register requires a per-trial denominator, this entry should be flagged "pooled, trial identities not recoverable".

MANDATORY CAVEATS to carry alongside the correction:
(a) TARGET-IS-EFFICACY PARTIAL CONFOUND: one of the seven pooled compounds (ION 696844) targets complement factor B. Bb is the activation fragment of factor B. The paper does not separate this compound in any complement analysis, so for an unknown fraction of the pooled Bb data, complement is an efficacy readout, not a toxicity readout. This does not invalidate the measurement but it contaminates the pooled Bb null.
(b) The measurement is narrow: two split products only (alternative-pathway Bb, terminal C5a); no C3/C4/C3a/sC5b-9, no functional assay; first dose only, 24 h window only; all-subcutaneous dosing, which is a weak test of the infusion-associated CARPA mechanism.
(c) Matrix, anticoagulant and assay are entirely unreported, so the measurement cannot be compared quantitatively with any other study, and the reference ranges are partly data-derived (mean +/- 2 SD of baselines where no range existed).
(d) "No evidence of complement activation" is the authors' wording for the pooled 24 h first-dose window. It is not evidence about chronic dosing, patient populations, or other GalNAc chemistries, and the supplement does contain one ASO-treated and one placebo Bb excursion >2 x ULN plus one unadjusted nominal p<0.05 that the main text does not mention.

compound_and_chemistry:
IN SCOPE as an oligonucleotide-based drug — and this is verified, not assumed. LJP 394 / abetimus sodium (later trade name Riquent; La Jolla Pharmaceutical Company, San Diego CA).

Construction, verbatim first-hand from Furie 2001 (PMID 11246659, p.257, full PDF read): "LJP 394 is an investigational drug under development as a selective B lymphocyte immunomodulator for the treatment of SLE. It is water soluble and has a molecular weight of 54 kDa. It consists of 4 double stranded 20-mer oligodeoxynucleotides attached through an aliphatic linkage to an inert scaffold composed of a triethyleneglycol core."

Synthesis and SEQUENCE, verbatim first-hand from the J Med Chem chemistry paper abstract (Jones DS et al., PMID 7783145): "A discrete tetravalent conjugate, 7a (LJP 394), consisting of four oligonucleotides attached to a common carrier or platform was prepared. Single-stranded oligonucleotide 20-mers consisting of alternating deoxycytidine-deoxyadenosine nucleotides, (CA)10, were attached to a tetrabromoacetylated platform by displacement with sulfhydryl-terminated linkers. The tetrabromoacetylated platform 3a was synthesized in three steps using triethylene glycol bis-(chloroformate)... The tetrakis, single-stranded conjugate was annealed with a stoichiometric amount of a complementary single-stranded oligonucleotide 20-mer consisting of alternating thymidine-deoxyguanosine nucleotides, (TG)10."

So: A SEQUENCE IS PUBLISHED — 5'-(CA)10-3' annealed to 5'-(TG)10-3', i.e. four identical 20-bp B-form DNA duplexes.

SCOPE CALL — it is NOT a protein/polymer conjugate, so the lead's out-of-scope worry does not apply. The scaffold is a small synthetic triethylene-glycol-derived tetravalent linker platform, not a protein (no KLH, no albumin) and not a macromolecular polymer carrier. Mass accounting: total 54 kDa; four 20-bp DNA duplexes are ~12.3 kDa each, i.e. ~49 kDa (~90%) of the molecule is synthetic oligodeoxynucleotide. Independent sponsor language, verbatim: "Abetimus sodium is an oligonucleotide-based investigational drug" (Linnik MD et al., J Clin Pharmacol 2008, PMID 18511650 abstract) and "a dsDNA-based bioconjugate (abetimus sodium; LJP 394)" (Linnik MD et al., Arthritis Rheum 2005, PMID 15818711 abstract). NLM indexes it under MeSH "Oligonucleotides/administration & dosage."

BACKBONE/SUGAR CHEMISTRY CAVEAT: no modified chemistry is reported in anything I read — it appears to be unmodified 2'-deoxyribose phosphodiester DNA. I did NOT read the J Med Chem full text, so the absence of any backbone modification is UNVERIFIED rather than confirmed. There is no 2'-MOE, no phosphorothioate, no GalNAc or lipid conjugate reported. Conjugate = tetravalent triethylene-glycol-bis(chloroformate)-derived platform, four arms, thioether (sulfhydryl-terminated linker displacing bromoacetyl) attachment.

MECHANISM CLASS CAVEAT worth carrying into the OligoTox catalogue: this is a B-cell TOLERAGEN that works by presenting dsDNA epitopes to cross-link surface Ig on anti-dsDNA-specific B cells. It is NOT antisense, NOT siRNA, NOT an aptamer, NOT an immunostimulatory CpG agonist. Its intended pharmacology is to form small immune complexes with circulating anti-dsDNA IgG — which is precisely why complement activation was a prespecified hazard here. Any read-across from this compound to a conventional single-stranded modified-backbone oligonucleotide should be treated as weak.

result_direction:
POSITIVE SIGNAL for complement activation, clinically silent, uncontrolled, unquantified. Direction = transient INCREASE in an unspecified subset of complement split products following a single 100 mg IV infusion in 4 SLE patients, with no accompanying adverse clinical events during or immediately after infusion. The authors attribute it mechanistically to in vivo immune-complex formation between drug and circulating anti-dsDNA IgG followed by rapid clearance.

What is NOT established, and must not be filled in: which split products rose; magnitude; time to peak and time to resolution (only "transient"); how many of the 4 patients; whether any value exceeded an assay reference range; and whether any native complement component fell. There is also no statistical testing possible at n=4 single-arm.

Separately, at the native-component level the programme direction is the OPPOSITE: no complement consumption, and C3/C4 rose. Verified first-hand in Furie 2001 (+14.1%/+15.9% mean C3 and +23.3%/+27.5% mean C4 at Weeks 16/18, 50 mg weekly), and reported in the later trial abstracts ("C3 levels tended to increase during treatment with LJP 394", PMID 12571854; "reductions in anti-dsDNA levels were associated with increases in C3 levels (P < 0.0001)", PMID 18668592). These two things are reconcilable and should be catalogued as such: an acute, infusion-locked rise in activation fragments can coexist with a chronic rise in native C3/C4 driven by reduced autoantibody-mediated consumption.

counting_rationale:
COUNT IT, as a LOW-STRENGTH, ABSTRACT-ONLY human complement-activation signal — and carry the caveats, because they are large.

Why it counts: the citation is verified first-hand against the NCBI MEDLINE record; it is a PubMed-typed Clinical Trial in humans; the drug is verified as genuinely oligonucleotide-based (~90% of its 54 kDa mass is synthetic dsDNA on a small triethylene-glycol linker platform, published sequence (CA)10/(TG)10, not a protein conjugate); complement split products were deliberately measured; and the author-stated direction is an increase. It is, as far as I can establish, the ONLY human study in the entire LJP 394 / abetimus programme that measured complement ACTIVATION products rather than native C3/C4 abundance. That makes it worth cataloguing even though it is thin.

Why its weight must be capped:
1. Full text could not be read — no online version of the article exists anywhere (see access_outcome). Everything about the complement result rests on one sentence of an author-written abstract.
2. The actual analytes are UNVERIFIED. "Some complement split products" is not an analyte list. No C3a / Bb / iC3b / SC5b-9 can be attributed.
3. Matrix and anticoagulant are NOT REPORTED. For split-product assays this is close to disqualifying on its own: improper collection produces exactly this "transient increase" pattern as an ex vivo artefact, and I cannot rule that in or out.
4. n=4, single-arm, no placebo, no statistics, no magnitudes, no timings.

TOXICITY vs DISEASE-ACTIVITY MONITORING — the confounder the lead asked me to address head-on. My read is that in THIS study the complement measurement is genuinely TOXICITY/hazard monitoring, not disease-activity monitoring, and here is the specific evidence rather than an assumption. The prespecified hazard was that the drug would bind circulating anti-dsDNA IgG and form immune complexes that fix complement — i.e. a drug-mechanism-driven infusion hazard. The companion trial states this concern explicitly and verbatim: "Despite prestudy concerns of complications arising secondary to in vivo immune complex formation between drug and autoantibody, the infusions were well tolerated." The 1997 design matches hazard monitoring rather than disease monitoring: a single dose, patients selected for STABLE SLE, a short 4-week window, split products (acute activation markers with half-lives of minutes to hours) rather than native C3/C4 (slow disease-activity markers), and a result described as time-locked to the infusion ("during or immediately after infusion"). Complement is NOT the drug's target, so this is NOT a target_is_complement_efficacy situation.

BUT the confounder is real and only partly controlled. Lupus patients consume complement from their disease, and SLE activity fluctuates spontaneously. The "stable SLE" entry criterion, the single-dose acute time course and the within-patient design mitigate this; the total absence of a placebo arm at n=4 means spontaneous disease-driven fluctuation in split products CANNOT be excluded as the explanation for a transient rise. Baseline complement status of the four women is UNVERIFIED — if any had active hypocomplementaemia, their split products would already be elevated and drifting.

CRITICAL CROSS-TRIAL WARNING for the catalogue: the same analyte family flips role across this programme. In the 1997 single-dose study, rising complement activation = possible HARM. In every later trial, rising native C3 = BENEFIT, used as a disease-activity/efficacy biomarker — verbatim registered intent, "Secondary objectives included evaluation of the effect of abetimus on C3 levels" (PMID 18668592), and "reductions in anti-dsDNA levels were associated with increases in C3 levels (P < 0.0001)". Do NOT pool the 1997 split-product result with the C3 results from Alarcón-Segovia 2003, Cardiel 2008 or Linnik 2005; and do not score the later C3 rises as "no complement toxicity," because those trials never measured activation products at all.

Finally: the 24-subject healthy-volunteer study at 600-2400 mg IV (PMID 18511650) — the one population with no lupus confounder and the highest doses in the programme — does not mention complement anywhere in its abstract. That is UNREPORTED, not negative, and it is the most valuable missing datapoint in this lead.

Direction for the 2'-modified ribo analogues: attenuated - less complement effect than PS-DNA. Senior author Agrawal's own 2021 retrospective (Biomedicines 2021;9:503, PMC8147625) cites this paper as its reference [40] and states verbatim: "We observed that 2'PS-modified ORNs had minimal effect on complement activation and prolongation of aPTT and also had reduced inflammatory responses [40]" - consistent, but second-hand and self-citing. Caution: "inhibits complement lysis" is phrased as inhibition of lysis, which is a marker of complement ACTIVATION/consumption, not of complement blockade - do not mis-score the sign.

counting_rationale:
Two separate reasons it should not be counted as a verified trial, and a third reason it should not even be counted as an independent human-laboratory source.

(1) NOT A TRIAL. This is an in vitro / ex vivo experiment on human blood material. No human subject received an oligonucleotide. Human-derived matrix is not a clinical trial, so counts_as_verified_trial = false. It does legitimately qualify as evidence_class = human_laboratory.

(2) NOT READ FIRST-HAND. Everything substantive here comes from the abstract plus bibliographic metadata. The matrix, anticoagulant, assay identity, oligonucleotide sequences, concentrations and donor numbers are all unverified. Confidence is abstract_only.

(3) NOT AN INDEPENDENT EXPERIMENT - this is the same group and the same program as Shaw 1997 and Agrawal 1995. This is the central finding for your dedup question, and the overlap is complete, not partial:
  - Lead (1998, PMID 9873494): Kandimalla ER, Shaw DR, Agrawal S - Hybridon Inc. (Kandimalla, Agrawal) + UAB (Shaw).
  - "Shaw 1997" = PMID 9175717, Shaw DR, Rustagi PK, Kandimalla ER, Manning AN, Jiang Z, Agrawal S. Biochem Pharmacol 1997;53(8):1123-32, "Effects of synthetic oligonucleotides on human complement and coagulation" - Shaw at UAB, with Kandimalla and Agrawal. Same three authors as the lead, plus Rustagi, Manning and Jiang.
  - "Agrawal 1995" = PMID 8597089, Agrawal S, Rustagi PK, Shaw DR. Toxicol Lett 1995;82-83:431-4, "Novel enzymatic and immunological responses to oligonucleotides" - Hybridon, with Shaw.
  - Also in the same cluster: PMID 8931938, Yu D, Iyer RP, Shaw DR, ... Agrawal S. Bioorg Med Chem 1996;4(10):1685-92, which already reported that 2'-O-methyl hybrid oligos "showed significantly reduced effect on complement activation".
  Note the near-identical titles of the 1997 and 1998 papers ("Effects of synthetic oligonucleotides on human complement and coagulation" vs "Effects of phosphorothioate oligodeoxyribonucleotide and oligoribonucleotides on human complement and coagulation"), the same two endpoints (hemolytic complement + aPTT), and the same Shaw hemolytic-complement capability at UAB. The lead is best treated as a short follow-up Letter extending the 1996/1997 work to a ribonucleotide chemistry panel, using the same assay lineage in the same laboratory.

RECOMMENDED COUNTING: do NOT add this as a fourth independent human-laboratory source. Collapse Agrawal 1995 + Shaw 1997 + Kandimalla 1998 (+ Yu 1996 if you are tracking it) into ONE Hybridon/UAB human-laboratory cluster, and keep Mangsbo 2009 and Sewing 2017 as the genuinely independent human-laboratory sources. The lead's distinct contribution within that cluster is the chemistry contrast (PS-DNA worse than PS-RNA / 2'-O-methyl-RNA / 2'-5'-RNA), not an independent replication. Whether the DNA arm is literally the same oligonucleotide and the same assay run as in Shaw 1997 is UNVERIFIED without the full text - but assume dependence, not independence.

Also flag: the compounds are antisense agents, not complement-targeting drugs, so complement here is a toxicity/safety endpoint, correctly in scope for this endpoint. And the attenuated effect of the 2'-modified RNA analogues is a reported comparative finding, not an "unreported = negative" inference.

readout_class: component_abundance — and only by proxy. The readout is presence/recovery of INTACT complement proteins in the aptamer-bound fraction of a plasma pull-down, read out by proteomic identification. It is explicitly NOT activation_split_product (no C3a/C5a/Bb/sC5b-9), NOT function (no CH50/haemolytic or Wieslab-type pathway assay), and NOT deposition. In other words: binding-partner inventory plus GO-style annotation, interpreted by the authors as "involved in complement activation". Identification of a complement component in a corona does not establish that convertase-mediated cleavage occurred.
compound_and_chemistry: Lead compound: AS1411 — a 26-nucleotide guanine-rich single-stranded DNA G-quadruplex aptamer whose target is nucleolin (NCL). Sequence per the Aptagen database entry that cites this exact paper: 5'-GGTGGTGGTGGTTGTGGTGGTGGTGG-3', listed there as unmodified phosphodiester DNA ("Chemical Modifications: None listed") — FLAGGED AS SECONDARY-SOURCE: this sequence was read from Aptagen, not from the paper itself, and is the canonical AS1411 sequence rather than a sequence I verified in the primary text. Per the abstract the authors also made "a series of optimizations ... via the chemical modifications of AS1411 aptamer", of which 3'-TERMINAL PEGYLATION was the variant shown to resist FN1 interaction and to improve tumour targeting. The abstract further says they "systematically studied" aptamer–plasma interactions with "structure-selective and sequence-specific" features, which implies a panel of several additional aptamers (DNA and/or RNA) — but the identities, sequences, lengths, backbone chemistry (phosphodiester vs phosphorothioate), sugar chemistry (DNA vs 2'-OMe/2'-F), conjugates and labels of that panel are ALL UNVERIFIED, as is the exact PEG chemistry and molecular weight. No sequence other than AS1411 is published in the accessible record. Class: aptamer (structured oligonucleotide), NOT an antisense/siRNA/GalNAc therapeutic.

result_direction: No complement activation result exists in this paper — neither positive nor negative. There is no activation measurement to have a direction. The only complement-related finding is that plasma proteins annotated to the "complement activation" pathway were over-represented among the proteins that bound the aptamers in a pull-down. This is a statement about BINDING-PARTNER COMPOSITION, not about convertase activity, split-product generation or terminal-complex formation. Explicitly: the absence of a C3a/C5a/Bb/sC5b-9 result must NOT be read as a negative complement finding — unreported is not negative. The paper's actual directional result is efficacy-directional and runs the other way from our endpoint: plasma protein binding (chiefly FN1) REDUCED aptamer target engagement, and 3'-PEGylation restored it.

counting_rationale: DECISIVE ANSWER TO THE LEAD'S CENTRAL QUESTION: this is (b), not (a). It is corona/interactome PROTEOMICS with pathway annotation, NOT a measurement of complement activation caused by the aptamer. It should NOT enter the endpoint's measurement tables, and it must not be counted as a complement-activation observation. Four independent reasons: (1) Readout mismatch — the paper identifies intact plasma proteins that CO-PRECIPITATE with aptamers; it quantifies no activation product (no C3a, C5a, Bb or sC5b-9) and performs no functional complement assay. Finding C3 or C1q in an oligonucleotide's protein corona is not evidence that C3 was cleaved; "complement activation" here is a Gene-Ontology-style label on the bound protein set, which is exactly the conflation this lead was written to catch. (2) Framing mismatch — the study's purpose is loss of TARGETING EFFICACY in the physiological milieu; the protein it actually follows up is fibronectin 1, not a complement component, and its remedy (3'-PEGylation) is validated by tumour targeting, not by any immune or complement readout. (3) Not a trial and not a human exposure — no registry, no protocol, no prespecified outcome, no human administration; human plasma was used as an ex vivo reagent, with the in vivo arm in animals. So it is not a human clinical observation under any reading, and I have classified it human_laboratory-derived material but mechanistic_only as evidence. (4) Verification floor not met — I could not read the full text (closed access plus a Cloudflare technical block), so even the weaker claim "no complement assay was performed" is only abstract-level; it is recorded as UNVERIFIED rather than asserted.
